summary: 1935 Coos Fire Patrol lookout in the Elliott State Forest; present 50-ft tower dates from 1966; last active 1985; standing but unsafe, unstaffed.

facts.design: 50-foot treated timber tower with live-in cab (present); first structure a 30-foot L-4 wooden tower
facts.status_note: Still standing but described as dilapidated and unsafe, and listed as abandoned; not used since 1985

access.note: No official open or closed notice found. The Education Center calls the tower unsafe for visitors, and the access road had no gate in 2024.

visit.trail_note: Park at the bottom of the access road and walk. A 2022 visitor found fallen trees and snow on the road. The tower is described as unsafe; do not climb it.

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry/Coos FPA per NHLR; Education Center says Department of State Lands manages it for the Common School Fund

corrections.why: The present tower is 50 feet (15.2 m) per NHLR. The 12.2 m figure (40 feet) matches the 1935 tower that the present one replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1936 for the first structure. A December 1935 Coos Bay Times item reports the new tower completed, and ORWW gives 1935. The story uses 1935 and states the register's 1936 date.
NHLR gives no date for the present 50-foot tower. The Coos district annual report (quoted by Forest Lookouts) and Cheryl Hill both date it to 1966.

notes_for_editor: The 1935 Coos Bay Times item and the 1940, 1945 and 1966 newspaper and annual-report entries were read only as quoted on Forest Lookouts, not from the originals. NHLR says the present tower is a 50-foot timber tower but gives no date for it. Status is abandoned per the June 2024 visit and standing per NHLR; both are kept. Administration conflicts: NHLR lists ODF/Coos FPA, the Education Center says DSL manages it for the Common School Fund; not resolved. No official open or closed notice was found, so access is marked restricted as our reading. Brief's height_m 12.2 corrected to 15.2. The Roaming Civic blog is used only for road number and gate pole. No new photos recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the register's administrator line reads Oregon Department of Forestry/Coos FPA; Coos Forest Protective Association is listed only as a cooperator, so the story no longer names it as administrator.
